newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Sharif makes economy top priority.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Sharif makes economy top priority.

text.p: Pakistans newly elected National Assembly (lower house of parliament) formally opened on Saturday with oath-taking by its deputies and pious vows by main political rivals.

"My top priority will be to bring the deteriorating economy back on the rails," prime minister-in-waiting Nawaz Sharif, whose Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party won a landslide in the February 3 elections, told reporters after taking the oath at Islamabads majestic parliament house.

His arch-rival, former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, who blames alleged vote-rigging for the rout of her Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), said she would allow the majority party to complete its term of government.
Pakistans constitution sets a five-year term of office for a prime minister, but all four premiers since 1985 have been prematurely sacked by presidents, mainly on disputed grounds of corruption.

Sharif, whom the PML formally named on Friday as its candidate for prime minister to be elected by the 217-seat National Assembly on Monday, said his government would work for Pakistan's prosperity and the uplift of the common man.

The PML and its small allied parties won a more than two-thirds majority in the assembly compared to only 19 seats for the PPP, which led a majority coalition in the previous house that was dismissed by President Farooq Leghari on November 5.

Bhutto has refused to accept the election results but says she will not undermine Pakistans stabliity. "The politics of conspiracy should end to stabilise the economy and the political system," she said on Saturday.

The oath to protect and defend Pakistans constitution has a controversial provision inserted by the late military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq that empowers a president to dismiss the assembly and sack a prime minister.
Sharif, 47, is certain to be elected prime minister because of his overwhelming majority, but the PPP on Friday named former defence minister Aftab Shaban Mirani as his rival for a token contest.
Sharif first became prime minister in 1990 after winning an election that also followed a dismissal of Bhutto's government by then president Ghulam Ishaq Khan on disputed corruption charges.
His government was dismissed by Ishaq two and half years later on similar charges, but was restored 35 days later by the Supreme Court, which held the presidential action to be illegal.
Sharif and Ishaq Khan both resigned later in an army-brokered deal for a fresh election, which Bhutto won.
Last month, the Supreme Court rejected Bhuttos plea for a restoration of her government and upheld the presidential action.
